theAnswerOnWhat48491ShouldServe.theQuestion: Two keyspaces name the same parcels -- the numeric declared-roll accounts (319,480 served, live, untouched by the 2026-09-17 run) and the R-prefixed parcel-index ids (282,569-282,570 served, every one of them falsely retired by writer (a) on 2026-09-17). What is the published end state?
theAnswerOnWhat48491ShouldServe.theAnswer: ONE KEYS PACE OF NODE IDENTITY PLUS A DECLARED ALIAS, and NOT a retirement of either -- the numeric keyspace is the county's ACCOUNT numbering and the R keyspace is the parcel-map index's own numbering, and the published end state is: every key of both keyspaces present in the fact build, with the ALIAS between them declared from the county's own published pair on the row, and no row of either retired for the other's absence.
theEvidence: `txgio_parcel` (the county's published parcel index, the parcel-map id's own keyspace) holds R-prefixed prop_ids and ZERO numeric ids for 48491 -- 304,162 in staging (this lane's read, 2026-09-19) / 282,569 in production (P-350's record). The R form IS the published parcel index's numbering.

The numeric keyspace is the CAD roll's numbering: `cad_property.prop_id` for 48491 is the six-digit account, and P-327 measured all 319,480 served numeric keys present on the declared 2026 roll -- they are live accounts, not hollow nodes.

The county itself publishes the relation between the two: `tx_wcad_owner` / `tx_wcad_ag_valuation` carry (prop_id = the R account the parcel index publishes, wcad_property_id = the numeric account the roll is keyed by), and P-351 measured the pair reaching 282,146 of the 282,570 published R keys (99.85%) with zero disagreements between the two extracts.

THE PRECEDENT THE DISPATCH NAMES, applied: `hays-node-id-is-the-parcel-map-id` -- the node id is the parcel-map id, the account joins ONLY through the crosswalk and never by bare number. Williamson's parcel-map id is the R form (it is the only form the parcel index publishes), so the R keyspace is the identity and the numeric keyspace is the account.

The customer lookup paths the dispatch names are both numeric (`48491:107190`, the walk gold `48491:76149`), and they resolve TODAY because the numeric keyspace is served -- which is why the answer cannot be 'retire the numeric keyspace': that would take the county's live served surface away from the lookups the product actually gets asked for.
theAnswerOnWhat48491ShouldServe.whatThatMeansInOneSentence: Both keyspaces are served; the R keyspace is the parcel-map identity; the numeric keyspace is the account, joined only through the county's own published pair; and a P-370 bake must therefore retire NEITHER for the other's absence -- it must decline to serve a false absence and instead DECLARE the alias it could not complete.
theAnswerOnWhat48491ShouldServe.whyThisDoesNotNeedTheOperator: It is not a new ruling, it is the precedent the dispatch cites plus the county's own published identifiers: the pair is the county's statement of which account belongs to which published parcel, and the parcel index is the county's statement of which parcels exist. Nothing in the fix chooses between the two keyspaces -- it stops ONE writer from deleting either on a comparison between them. Whether the numeric keyspace should EVENTUALLY be retired with the R form as its named successor, or kept as a served alias forever, is a product decision that this lane does not take and does not need to take: BOTH end states require that the bake first stop refusing, and neither is made harder by this change.
theAnswerOnWhat48491ShouldServe.whatWouldNeedTheOperator: Only a decision to REMOVE the numeric keyspace from the served surface (a serve-path change, P-297-shaped, outside this repo's bake). Named here so the integration seat knows which question is still open rather than discovering it.

theTwoEndStatesAndWhyTheFirstWasRejected.whyThisSectionExists: The dispatch says 'a node no published identifier reaches is DECLARED (not retired, not excluded as hollow)'. The first cut of this lane's fix honored the first clause and violated the second, and the measurement is what caught it. Both end states are recorded with their counts so the next reader can see why the shipped one is the shipped one.

endStateA_theFirstCut_REJECTED.rule: The bare-key test decides hollowness; the county's published pair is consulted as a SECOND arm that moves a key back into the fact build when the pair names it to a prop_id this county's parcel table publishes. A key the pair does not reach stays excluded (retired), with the retirement record's scope widened to name the pair that did not reach it.
endStateA_theFirstCut_REJECTED.measured: 319,480 numeric keys excluded before the fix -> 282,146 moved back by the pair -> 37,334 STILL EXCLUDED, i.e. retired.
endStateA_theFirstCut_REJECTED.whyItIsWrong: Those 37,334 are live numeric keys on the declared 2026 roll (P-327's count: all 319,480 served numeric keys are present on the declared roll), so the run would have written 37,334 false retirements -- the exact class of write P-351 exists to prevent -- and P-351's guard CANNOT see it: the guard is SET EQUALITY against a whole served keyspace, and 37,334 of 319,480 (11.7%) is not a whole keyspace, so the refusal would not fire and the write would land. A narrower version of the same defect, on 11.7% of a live keyspace instead of 100%.
endStateA_theFirstCut_REJECTED.theLesson: A guard that is set equality against a whole keyspace does not protect a keyspace from a partial extraction, and an arm that moves keys back into the build is not the same thing as a test that declines to exclude on a premise it cannot check.

endStateB_THE_SHIPPED_RULE.rule: In a county that PUBLISHES a pair over this run's account-shaped keys, the bare-key test is not admissible for those keys at all. A key on the declared roll whose published pair names it to a published prop_id is a served parcel (kept, and it is counted); a key the pair does not reach is DECLARED -- KEPT IN THE BUILD, not retired, with the declaration made by the arm that already makes declarations for a node whose account cannot be resolved (writer (a)'s `retirementResolution`, P-351). Nothing in the account-shaped keyspace is excluded as hollow, so nothing is retired on a comparison between two keyspaces.
endStateB_THE_SHIPPED_RULE.whyItIsTheDispatchsSentence: 'A node the pair maps to a published parcel is not hollow. A node no published identifier reaches is DECLARED (not retired, not excluded as hollow).' End state B is that sentence, both clauses.
endStateB_THE_SHIPPED_RULE.whatItCostsAndWhyThatCostIsTheRightOne: A key that genuinely left the roll and that the pair does not name is NOT retired; it is declared and stays served. That is a DECLARED ABSENCE where a retirement would have been available -- and the program's law is that a declared absence beats a false absence, and that a number on the card names its SHA (NOTHING IS MEASURED ONCE AND PUBLISHED AS STATE). It is also the direction that is reversible: a later lane can retire a declared key on better evidence; it cannot un-retire a row it emptied.
endStateB_THE_SHIPPED_RULE.whatItDoesNotTouch: A county that publishes NO pair over this run's account-shaped keys (Hays 48209: its pair read returns rows for zero of its numeric keys) keeps the pre-P-370 verdict EXACTLY -- same exclusion, key for key. The guard stays and still fires: a whole-keyspace exclusion still refuses, and a pair that reaches nothing leaves the exclusion whole.

legacyDesignTools: src/lib/accountKeyedWork.ts (EDIT). `isAccountKeyedNodeId` / `partitionAccountKeyedWork` gain the county's published pair READ BY THE ACCOUNT (node key -> the parcel-index prop_id the pair names for it) as an OPTIONAL second input, and gain the third verdict: a key of a county whose pair is live for this run is 'declared', not 'hollow'. The partition returns counts, not only sets: how many keys the pair named to a published prop_id (the population the arm moved back into the fact build), and how many are declared rather than excluded. `accountKeyedBlastRadius` / `assertAccountKeyedBlastRadius` are UNCHANGED -- the guard is not weakened, it is consulted on a partition that no longer contains a whole keyspace.

src/lib/retirementAccountResolution.ts (EDIT). `buildPublishedNodeKeyByAccountKey` -- the same published pair `buildPublishedAccountPair` already builds, read in the OTHER direction (account key -> node key), by delegating to it with the roles swapped so the two can never disagree about a key, and inheriting its refusals (a key an extract carries with no counterpart is refused and counted; one extract naming a key twice is refused as ambiguous; two extracts naming different counterparts refuse the key rather than winning a coin toss).

src/lib/joinIntegrityGate.ts (EDIT). `fetchPublishedAccountPairExtractsByAccount` -- the indexed read of the county's own staged extracts by the ACCOUNT column, chunked, returning the rows plus which sources were present and which were absent, so a run that read nothing says so.

src/nodeFacetBakeTier1ConformantCli.ts (EDIT). Asks the pair read ONLY for the keys the first arm is about to exclude AND whose shape is the account shape the pair is keyed by (so a county whose exclusion is already empty adds no query, and a one-keyspace county asks for nothing); hands the map to the partition ONLY when the read returned rows; prints the pair statistics and the per-keyspace line; and carries the new counters into the run's JSON summary so a run in which the arm did nothing is legible from outside rather than discovered from a refusal.
The tests: the falsifiers below, in the two suites that already hold writer (b)'s and the resolution's instruments.
whatIWillBuild.whatIWillNotDo: No store write, no bake apply, no publish, no deploy, no merge, no sub-agent. The dry runs are `--dry-run` against the STAGING stores under this lane's own heavy-scan lease, one window at a time. The factory pin is NOT moved by this lane (the integration seat moves `_LDT_SHA` when it merges).

preRegisteredFalsifiers: F1 WILLIAMSON'S NUMERIC KEYSPACE IS NO LONGER EXCLUDED, AND THE COUNT IS PREDICTED. A fixture with the measured shape (a numeric keyspace, a pair naming most of it to published prop_ids, one key whose pair row names a prop_id this county's parcel table does NOT publish, one key named by nothing) must show: with the pair, the per-keyspace line reads the predicted excluded count (1 of 3 in the scaled fixture; 0 of 319,480 in the real dry run) and the partition reports the count it moved; without it, the same fixture refuses. Would falsify the fix if the reachable key stayed excluded, or if the count disagreed with the prediction. BOTH DIRECTIONS are asserted in one test, because the second arm is optional and the same fixture can be run both ways.

F2 HAYS' HOLLOW SET IS UNCHANGED KEY FOR KEY. A golden list, pinned in the test, of the keys writer (b) excludes in the measured Hays shape -- with no map, with a map that names none of them, and with a CROSS-COUNTY map that names them to Williamson R prop_ids the Hays parcel table does not publish (the two-source collision the reverse builder is NOT trusted to resolve on its own). All three runs must produce the identical list. Would falsify the fix if a county that publishes no pair lost a single exclusion.

F3 A FIXTURE WHOSE WHOLE KEYSPACE MISSES THE PARCEL TABLE STILL REFUSES. The guard is proven able to fire on the shipped code, not merely declared intact: a pair that reaches nothing (empty map, and a map whose every row names an unpublished prop_id) leaves the whole-keyspace exclusion whole and `assertAccountKeyedBlastRadius` still throws.

F4 A SINGLE-KEYSPACE COUNTY'S PAYLOAD IS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO BEFORE. P-351's golden-hash method, extended to this change: a retirement record built with no second published identifier must serialise to the same bytes it wrote before P-370, asserted as the EXACT string, not merely as 'contains'. Would falsify the fix if declaring the third verdict had changed what a county with no pair writes.

F5 THE PAIR READ IS COUNTED, NOT ASSUMED. The reverse builder's three refusal paths (no prop_id carried, one extract naming a key twice, two extracts disagreeing) are each asserted to refuse and to be counted, and the reverse map is asserted to be the forward map's inverse over the same rows -- so the two directions are one instrument, not two opinions.

F6 THE THREE-QUESTION GATE, ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN BY READING. What executes the membership test, what triggers it, what fails when a live keyspace is excluded, and what bypasses it -- answered in the close from the run's own output (the per-keyspace line before and after) and from the call sites, not from the intention.

theThreeQuestionGateAsDesigned.whatExecutesWriterBsMembershipTest: `partitionAccountKeyedWork` (src/lib/accountKeyedWork.ts), called from `nodeFacetBakeTier1ConformantCli.ts`'s account-keyed prepass, once per run, over the run's own work list; the verdict per key is `isAccountKeyedNodeId`. The blast-radius instrument over its result is `accountKeyedBlastRadius` + `assertAccountKeyedBlastRadius`, called BEFORE `work` is mutated.
theThreeQuestionGateAsDesigned.whatTriggersIt: `joinGateBlocked && parcelTable` -- a gate-blocked county whose bake holds a parcel table. It runs INSIDE the bake, after promotion, on the work list the bake built and the run stamp the bake minted; the factory's pre-bake gate cannot see a single excluded node.
theThreeQuestionGateAsDesigned.whatFailsWhenALiveKeyspaceIsExcluded: Before P-351 it emptied the county: Williamson's 2026-09-17 publish retired all 282,570 published R nodes while 319,480 live numeric rows sat beside them, and the write reads as an EARNED absence with an authority, so it reads as a fact about the parcel rather than as a failed lookup. Since P-351 it refuses instead, which is the state this lane found: the county cannot publish at all. What fails is either way the county's served surface -- emptied, or frozen.
whatBypassesIt: A direct invocation of the bake CLI outside the publish job -- which is why the guard lives in the bake and not in the gate.
Structurally, a county whose work list already excludes the nodes before the prepass could see them.

THE 37,334 (measured shape) numeric keys the county's pair does not name, and the 424 published R nodes the pair does not name: under the shipped rule both are DECLARED and neither is retired. If the integration seat wants a retirement signal for them, the signal must come from the declared roll (an account that left) and not from a comparison between two keyspaces -- and it is writer (a)'s resolution (P-351), not writer (b), that owns the declared roll.
